Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Wheeze and shortness of breath for 2 days.
- History of presenting complaint:
  - Onset: Began ~2 days ago after cleaning house and exposure to dust.
  - Course/progression: Started about an hour after exposure; symptoms have worsened over the 2 days and are worse at night.
  - Symptoms: Wheeze, shortness of breath, difficulty completing sentences when talking; no chest pain, no dizziness.
  - Triggers: Patient reports possible dust allergy; history of hay fever.
  - Self-treatment: None taken for current episode.
- Past medical history:
  - Childhood asthma (mostly resolved; exercise can occasionally trigger symptoms).
  - Seasonal hay fever in summer.
- Previous medications/surgeries:
  - Has an asthma inhaler at home (asthma inhaler — dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - History of prior steroid use for asthma (oral steroids — dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social history:
  - Proximity to GP: a few minutes' drive from clinic/surgery.
- Allergies:
  - Patient reports no known allergies ("not that I know of").

Objective:
- Physical examination: No physical examination documented in the transcript.
- Vitals: Not recorded in the transcript.
- Investigations:
  - Pulse oximetry (finger oximeter) planned to be performed at an in-person clinic visit; not yet performed.

1. Wheeze/shortness of breath:
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Possible asthma exacerbation
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Allergic reaction to dust (allergic-induced bronchospasm)
     - Recurrent or adult-onset asthma symptoms
     - Other causes of wheeze (not specified)
   - Investigations planned:
     - Pulse oximetry (finger oximeter) at clinic
     - Further in-person assessment and testing as indicated (details not specified)
   - Treatment planned:
     - Recommend taking an over-the-counter antihistamine prior to clinic visit if symptoms likely allergy-related (patient does not currently have antihistamines at home).
     - Consider oral corticosteroids if indicated after in-person assessment and investigations (not initiated remotely).
   - Relevant referrals:
     - Letter to GP will be written and sent via app.
     - Patient advised to attend an in-person clinic/GP appointment for evaluation and tests.

   - Differential diagnosis: N/A (history)
   - Investigations planned:

   - Treatment planned:
